title: Network Security Basics Overview
content: Network Security Basics is a core foundational course on CyberLearn LMS by CyberDaksh. It covers essential computer networking concepts, defensive security architecture, protocols, and security monitoring techniques. Students learn how networks transmit data, how attackers exploit architectural weaknesses, and how defensive controls like firewalls, DMZs, and packet analyzers safeguard enterprise networks.

title: OSI & TCP/IP Reference Models
content: Module 1 of Network Security Basics covers the 7 layers of the OSI model (Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application) and the 4 layers of the TCP/IP stack. Students learn packet encapsulation/decapsulation, protocol data units (PDUs), port addressing (TCP/UDP), IP routing, and common protocols including HTTP, HTTPS, DNS, ARP, ICMP, and SSH.

module_name: Module 2 — Firewall Configuration & Access Control Lists
title: Firewall Configuration & ACLs
content: Module 2 of Network Security Basics explores firewall architectures and packet filtering. Key topics include: 1. Stateful vs. Stateless Packet Filtering (stateless checks static packet headers, stateful tracks TCP connection state in a session table). 2. Access Control Lists (ACLs) configuration based on source IP, destination IP, protocols, and port numbers. 3. Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW) with deep packet inspection (DPI) and application-layer awareness.

module_name: Module 3 — Network Packet Analysis with Wireshark
title: Network Packet Analysis with Wireshark
content: Module 3 of Network Security Basics teaches packet inspection using Wireshark and tcpdump. Students learn how to: 1. Capture live network traffic in virtual sandbox environments. 2. Inspect protocol packet headers and decode payload data. 3. Filter traffic using display filters (e.g., tcp.port == 80, ip.addr == 192.168.1.1). 4. Identify malicious traffic anomalies such as SYN floods, ARP spoofing, cleartext credential transmissions, and port scanning patterns.

module_name: Module 4 — Defensive Perimeter Security & DMZ Architecture
title: Defensive Perimeter Security & DMZ Architecture
content: Module 4 covers defensive network perimeter design. It includes Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) architecture for hosting public-facing servers (web, mail) while isolating internal enterprise subnets, Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS like Snort and Suricata), Virtual Private Networks (VPNs via IPsec/OpenVPN), and secure gateway routing.

title: Ethical Hacking & Penetration Testing Overview
content: The Ethical Hacking & Penetration Testing track provides hands-on offensive cybersecurity training. Students learn industry-standard penetration testing methodologies, vulnerability discovery, active/passive reconnaissance, exploitation frameworks, and professional remediation reporting within isolated cloud sandboxes using Kali Linux tools.

title: Reconnaissance & Footprinting
content: Module 1 of Ethical Hacking covers information gathering techniques. Students explore: 1. Passive Reconnaissance: OSINT, WHOIS lookups, DNS enumeration, search engine dorking, and certificate transparency logs. 2. Active Reconnaissance: Port scanning and service banner grabbing using Nmap, host discovery, OS fingerprinting, and vulnerability scanning with OpenVAS.

title: System Exploitation & Metasploit Framework
content: Module 2 focuses on controlled exploitation within isolated sandbox environments. Topics include: 1. Metasploit Framework: Exploit modules, auxiliary scanners, payloads (Meterpreter), and handlers. 2. Buffer overflow fundamentals and remote code execution concepts. 3. Post-exploitation privilege escalation (Linux sudo/SUID exploits, Windows token manipulation). 4. Ethical rules of engagement and non-destructive testing standards.

title: Web Application Security Overview
content: Web Application Security covers modern application threats, OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, API security, and secure coding practices. Students use Burp Suite Community/Pro in hands-on browser labs to intercept HTTP/S requests, discover injection vulnerabilities, bypass broken authentication, and implement defensive mitigations.

title: SQL Injection (SQLi) & OWASP Top 10
content: Module 1 delves into SQL Injection (SQLi) and injection flaws. Topics covered: 1. In-band SQLi (Union-based, Error-based), Blind SQLi (Boolean-based, Time-based), and Out-of-Band SQLi. 2. Database exfiltration and authentication bypass techniques. 3. Defensive remediation: Parameterized queries (Prepared Statements), Object Relational Mapping (ORM) safety, and input validation.

title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) & CSRF
content: Module 2 covers client-side attacks: 1. Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): Stored XSS, Reflected XSS, and DOM-based XSS. Mitigation via context-aware output encoding and Content Security Policy (CSP). 2. Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF): Session hijacking, unauthorized state-changing requests, and SameSite cookie attributes with anti-CSRF token verification.

title: CyberLearn Official Certification Requirements
content: To earn an official CyberLearn Verified Certificate of Completion from CyberDaksh, a student must fulfill all three criteria: 1. Course Module Completion: Complete 100% of all video lectures, reading materials, and interactive quizzes. 2. Practical Lab Submissions: Complete and submit all mandatory hands-on virtual lab exercises. 3. Final Assessment: Pass the comprehensive course final assessment with a minimum score of 75%. Upon meeting these requirements, a cryptographically signed CyberDaksh certificate is issued automatically to the learner profile.

title: CyberDaksh Internship Eligibility & Selection Criteria
content: CyberDaksh offers cybersecurity internship opportunities for top-performing CyberLearn students. Eligibility criteria: 1. Specialized Track Enrollment: The candidate must be actively enrolled in either the Ethical Hacking or Web Security track. 2. High Academic Standing: Maintain an 'A' grade with an overall average score of at least 85% across all module quizzes and labs. 3. Capstone Final Project: Successfully design, execute, and submit the end-of-track capstone security project reviewed by CyberDaksh security engineers.

title: CyberLearn Hands-On Cloud Virtual Labs
content: CyberLearn features dedicated browser-based virtual lab sandboxes. Each student gets an isolated, ephemeral containerized environment with pre-installed security tools including Wireshark, Nmap, Metasploit, Burp Suite, SQLmap, and Hydra. Labs run entirely in the browser via WebSockets and HTML5 canvas without requiring local virtualization or software installations.

title: Course Recommendations by Career Path
content: CyberLearn provides structured learning paths depending on your career goals: 1. Beginners & Foundation: Start with 'Network Security Basics' to master networking protocols, firewalls, and packet analysis. 2. Aspiring Penetration Testers / Red Teamers: Take 'Ethical Hacking & Penetration Testing' after Network Security to learn reconnaissance, Metasploit, and exploitation. 3. Web Developers & AppSec Engineers: Enroll in 'Web Application Security' to master OWASP Top 10, SQLi, XSS, and secure API architecture.
